text:
infra-bot: ALERT: ap-south1 runtime: kv RPC slowpath rate jumped to 35% | 99p latency ~1.1s (baseline 110ms) — error budget approaching. Auto-remediate not triggered yet :warning:
maya: seeing 5xxs and timeouts on a subset of NVMe-backed hosts, likely RPC retries to control plane. 99p tokens/req up, tail latency on text-gen spiking.
henry: I’m on it — checking node-level network metrics and dmesg. tagging relevant gpu pools.
ashley: @henry can we start traffic steering to na-west for latency-sensitive routes? we should keep embeddings in region.
henry: agree. prepping routing change. will do gradual 10% -> 30% -> 60% if metrics hold.
ops-sre: FYI cost impact estimate if we shift 60% of capacity to na-west: ~+12% core infra spend for next 12h.
maya: alternative short-term: force runtime to prefer local in-memory KV cache and reduce continuous batch size to avoid head-of-line stalls. cheaper than cross-region egress.
denielle: what flags do we have for that?
henry: runtime flags: `--kv-local-cache=enabled`, `--kv-fallback-retry-ms=200`, `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=384`, `CONTINUOUS_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS=8`.
maya: I'll prepare a canary config and roll to ap-south1 small subset (pool-az3) first.
router-bot: deploy plan created: `route-change: ap-south1 -> na-west (traffic=10%)` by henry at 1923456900.
henry: executing initial 10% steer now: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/v1/steer -d '{"from":"ap-south1","to":"na-west","pct":10}'` — pausing for metrics.
maya: rolling kv-local-cache toggle to pool-az3 now. patch: ```json
{"pool":"pool-az3","runtime_flags":{"kv_local_cache":"true","batch_max_tokens":384}}
```
ashley: patch applied, monitoring.
henry: initial 10% traffic shift looks ok, 99p latency for routed requests ~130ms. ap-south1 overall 99p only down 15% so far.
maya: can you check RPC histograms for kv-store? I see increased tail on GET latencies specifically hitting `kv-store-03` hosts.
ops-sre: pulled interface stats — rx drop counters jumped on io0 for three hosts. raising networking ticket with provider.
denielle: if provider indicates flapping we should keep partial steer and keep kv-local-cache on. also consider temporarily increasing cache TTL to reduce RPCs.
henry: increasing cache TTL to 45s on canary (was 5s) — doing now.
maya: after TTL bump + local cache we see 99p drop from 1.1s -> 260ms for canary. good signal.
henry: moving to 30% traffic steer. running curl again with pct=30.
ashley: routing logs show ~20% of sessions diverted; no error surge in na-west.
infra-bot: NOTE: fallback route uses quantized-small model variants for burst traffic if capacity tight.
ops-sre: cost note — using quantized variants increases throughput but may affect quality for some customers. need comms if we keep this >4h.
maya: quality impact is small for short prompts; acceptable for emergency. leaving fallback enabled.
denielle: any sign of KV-store host evictions? If hosts get evicted we need to rehydrate caches.
henry: not yet. provider says link flap on switch 12 in ap-south1; they’re applying firmware patch. ETA 25m.
maya: plan: keep kv-local-cache=true, batch_max_tokens=384, continuous_batch_interval=8ms, cache_ttl=45s for 30-60m; progressively shift traffic back once kv GET tail normalizes.
ashley: @ops-sre please prepare customer-facing note outlining region performance degradation and temporary traffic steering + quality fallback.
ops-sre: on it. draft will mention expected mitigation timeline ~30-45m.
henry: metrics at last check: ap-south1 99p down to 300ms, overall error rate back to baseline. moving to 60% steer in 10m if stable.
denielle: once provider confirms link stable, we should revert TTL and local cache to default to avoid cache staleness. schedule a graceful revert.
maya: agree. I’ll add revert job to deploy pipeline: `revert-kv-emergency` with preflight checks (RPC tail <150ms for 10m).
router-bot: scheduled `revert-kv-emergency` at 1923457600 if preflight passes.
henry: rolling 60% now. visual check looks clean.
ops-sre: cost update: current hour spend projection +14% vs baseline due to cross-region traffic and quantized model usage. still within burn for emergency.
ashley: thumbs on final revert plan. will keep customer comms short. :thumbsup:
maya: good job team. preserving these flags as emergency runbook notes. will open follow-up to investigate root cause of nvme host rx drops and consider traffic affinity improvements.
infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: ap-south1 kv RPC slowpath cleared after provider firmware patch and routing adjustments. duration ~47m. reopen if you see regressions. :white_check_mark:
